subsystem: wallet signing capabilities: FloFi Wallet (Privy embedded, @privy-io/react-auth 3.51.0), MetaMask/injected EVM (EIP-6963/EIP-1193), Phantom/Solflare (Wallet Standard)
summary: Path key: PRIVY = node_modules/.pnpm/@privy-io+react-auth@3.51.0_@solana-program+memo@0.16.0_@solana+kit@8.5.0_typescript@5._f88946ba1c9d593861eb622955a9774b/node_modules/@privy-io/react-auth. The installed Privy browser SDK can sign EIP-712 typed data with its own confirmation screen (useSignTypedData), sign EIP-1559 transactions without sending (useSignTransaction), and sign Solana transactions (useSignTransaction from /solana). It CANNOT batch EVM calls (no wallet_sendCalls: its embedded EIP-1193 provider sends unknown methods to the public RPC), CANNOT sign several Solana transactions in one prompt (the variadic hook loops and opens one confirmation screen per transaction), and can produce an EIP-7702 authorization only HEADLESSLY (useSign7702Authorization calls the raw-hash method secp256k1_sign, which has no Privy confirmation screen and no uiOptions). Its UnsignedTransactionRequest type has no authorizationList, so a Privy wallet cannot sign and pay a type-4 upgrade transaction itself. Privy smart wallets (useSmartWallets) need Privy dashboard configuration (smartWalletType + per-chain bundlerUrl), the optional peer dependency permissionless (not installed), and use a separate smart-account address of type safe/kernel/light_account/biconomy/coinbase_smart_wallet/thirdweb/nexus. The MetaMask EIP7702StatelessDeleGator type is not among them. FloFi's own FloFi Wallet surface (flofi-evm-provider.ts, flofi-solana-wallet.ts, flofi-privy-signer.ts, wallet-app/protocol.ts ops) allows only: one bound EIP-1559 eth_sendTransaction (FloFi broadcasts), personal_sign of FloFi's own sign-in text, wallet_switchEthereumChain among 4 mainnets, one bound Solana v0 transaction per solana:signTransaction call, and Solana sign-in messages. Every transaction signature is bound server-side to one PREPARED attempt of 10 single-run flows (SIGNING_FLOWS) and claimed once. Workflow-run groups, universal-router bridges and typed data are refused. Injected EVM wallets are discovered by EIP-6963 (legacy window.ethereum only when nothing announces), chosen explicitly, and switched with wallet_switchEthereumChain (+ wallet_addEthereumChain on 4902). The app already calls eth_signTypedData_v4 (workflow grants, credential delegations) but never wallet_getCapabilities, wallet_sendCalls or wallet_getCallsStatus. Solana wallets (Phantom, Solflare, ...) are found only through Wallet Standard registration by name. FloFi requires standard:connect + solana:signTransaction. signWithSolanaWallet passes exactly one input, and FloFi Wallet's own Solana wallet refuses inputs.length != 1.

answers.question: (1) Which EVM and Solana signing methods does the installed Privy SDK expose to the browser (embedded wallet)? Typed data, 7702 authorization, several Solana transactions in one call? Smart-wallet facility and its config dependency?
answers.answer: Installed version: @privy-io/react-auth 3.51.0 (apps/reference-dapp/package.json:24), with @privy-io/node 0.36.0 server side. EVM, for the embedded wallet: (a) personal_sign through useSignMessage / PrivyInterface.signMessage, with a confirmation screen. (b) EIP-712 eth_signTypedData_v4 through useSignTypedData / PrivyInterface.signTypedData, with a confirmation screen (SignRequestScreen; uiOptions = SignMessageModalUIOptions: title, description, buttonText, iconUrl, isCancellable, showWalletUIs). TypedMessage domain = {name, version, chainId:number, verifyingContract, salt}, which fits the MetaMask delegator PackedUserOperation typed data. YES, Privy can sign it. (c) eth_signTransaction through useSignTransaction (sign only, confirmation screen; FloFi already uses it). (d) eth_sendTransaction through useSendTransaction, which has a 'sponsor' flag (Privy gas sponsorship; FloFi must never use it). (e) EIP-7702: useSign7702Authorization({contractAddress, chainId?, nonce?, executor?}, {address}). It has NO uiOptions, and the implementation prepares the authorization with viem and signs its hash with the embedded provider's raw 'secp256k1_sign'. That method is routed straight to the wallet proxy / wallet API with no Privy confirmation screen: only eth_sendTransaction, eth_signTransaction, personal_sign and eth_signTypedData_v4 have UI handlers. So Privy CAN sign a 7702 authorization, but only headlessly, through an arbitrary-hash signing primitive. (f) UnsignedTransactionRequest has no authorizationList field, so a type-4 upgrade transaction cannot be signed with useSignTransaction (typed API; not verified at runtime). (g) The embedded EIP-1193 provider sends every method outside its switch and outside SUPPORTED_ETHEREUM_RPC_METHODS to the public RPC client. wallet_getCapabilities, wallet_sendCalls and wallet_getCallsStatus are therefore NOT supported: no EIP-5792 batching. Solana (@privy-io/react-auth/solana): useSignTransaction / useSignAndSendTransaction / useSignMessage are typed variadic (...inputs), but the implementation (solana.mjs function Ge) awaits one wallet.signTransaction per input. PrivyStandardWallet's solana:signTransaction also loops over the single-transaction injection, and each call (useWallets function lt) opens EmbeddedWalletConnectingScreen -> StandardSignAndSendTransactionScreen for ONE transaction. NO, Privy cannot sign several Solana transactions in one prompt: N inputs = N sequential Privy screens. useSignAndSendTransaction also has 'sponsor'. Smart wallets: @privy-io/react-auth/smart-wallets (SmartWalletsProvider, useSmartWallets -> client.sendTransaction(single or calls[]), signMessage, signTypedData, switchChain) is built on 'permissionless' (+ permissionless/accounts, permissionless/clients/pimlico). That is an OPTIONAL peer dependency and is NOT installed. It also needs Privy dashboard configuration (AppConfig.smartWallets from AppResponse.smart_wallet_config: enabled, smartWalletType, configuredNetworks[{chainId, bundlerUrl, paymasterUrl?}]); at runtime it throws 'must be configured in the smart wallet configuration in your dashboard'. SmartWalletType is one of safe, kernel, light_account, biconomy, coinbase_smart_wallet, thirdweb, nexus. There is no MetaMask EIP7702StatelessDeleGator, and the smart wallet is a separate contract address, not the owner's EOA. Session signers / delegated actions / policies also exist: useDelegatedActions.delegateWallet, useSessionSigners (deprecated), useSigners.addSigners({address, signers:[{signerId, policyIds?}]}), useAuthorizationSignature, useTransfer/useWalletActions. They give a server key quorum signing power under dashboard policies; FloFi explicitly excludes them.

answers.question: (2) What does FloFi Wallet's provider/signer/protocol allow and refuse, and where would a new op (EVM typed-data sign of a user operation, Solana sign-several) be added and bound to a reviewed run?
answers.answer: ALLOWED, EVM provider: eth_requestAccounts, eth_accounts, eth_chainId, net_version, wallet_switchEthereumChain among Base/Arbitrum/Ethereum/Robinhood (0x2105, 0xa4b1, 0x1, 0x1237); otherwise 4902. eth_getTransactionCount(own address, 'pending') through FloFi's server. personal_sign: UTF-8 text only, and the server accepts only FloFi's own sign-in message. eth_sendTransaction: one at a time, only with a binding taken from bindFloFiSigning; type-2 only (gasPrice/legacy refused); accessList, authorizationList and maxFeePerBlobGas refused; same chain; to/data/gas required; nonce/fees filled from the server when absent. Privy signs, the signed bytes are re-verified field by field, and FloFi broadcasts once. REFUSED: everything else, with 4200 FLOFI_WALLET_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED (eth_signTypedData_v4, eth_signTransaction for later use, wallet_sendCalls, wallet_getCapabilities, wallet_addEthereumChain -> 4200). Solana wallet: features solana:signTransaction (supportedTransactionVersions [0], EXACTLY one input, mainnet only, <=1232 bytes, bound run required, the result must be the same bytes with a non-zero slot-0 signature) and solana:signMessage (FloFi sign-in text only); no signAndSendTransaction. Privy signer (requestThroughPrivy): ops evm_sign_transaction, solana_sign_transaction (server gate floFiSigningGate first: resolves {flow, runId} to the run's PREPARED/SUBMITTING attempt, requires an owner among the account's Privy wallets and exactly these bytes, and claims the attempt's single signature), evm_sign_message, solana_sign_message (floFiMessageGate); any other op -> FLOFI_WALLET_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED. Protocol ops: connect, manage, create, import, export, evm_sign_transaction, evm_sign_message, solana_sign_transaction (single base64 <=2048 chars), solana_sign_message. The legacy popup is export-only today; the op types are reused as the Privy request vocabulary. Binding scope: SIGNING_FLOWS holds only 10 single-run flows (jupiter-swap, solana-transfer, 4 x *-mainnet-transfer, 4 x *-swap). The universal router (bridges) and solana-composition stores never call bindFloFiSigning, so FloFi Wallet refuses them (FLOFI_WALLET_FLOW_NOT_SUPPORTED). Workflow run ids (wfr_ + 26 base32 characters) do not even match the SigningContext RUN regex /^[a-z]{2,8}-[0-9a-f]{24,32}$/. WHERE TO ADD (both ops follow the same five layers): 1) protocol.ts: new WalletOperation variants 'evm_sign_user_operation' {op, address, chainId, typedData, signing} and 'solana_sign_transactions' {op, address, chain, transactions: base64[1..8], signing}, with exact-key strict parsers in parseOperation and new result shapes in parseWalletResponse ({signature} already fits; add {signedTransactions: string[]} with per-entry and total bounds); add both ops to SIGNING_OPS in flofi-wallet-channel.ts:38 so normalize requires a binding. 2) flofi-signing.ts: a group flow per ecosystem (resolveManagedSigning checks SIGNING_FLOWS[flow].ecosystem === request.ecosystem at managed-signing.ts:266), e.g. 'workflow-group-evm' / 'workflow-group-solana' with run /^wfg-[0-9a-f]{32}$/: a group id minted by the server per (runId, groupIndex), so parseSigningContext needs no widening. 3) Server: extend parseSigningRequest (managed-signing.ts:287-313) with the two shapes, and add a group resolver beside resolveManagedSigning (managed-signing.ts:263-280). It loads the group's FROZEN artifact (the PackedUserOperation fields or the N unsigned Solana messages), requires group state AWAITING_SIGNATURE, owner = an account Privy wallet, byte equality (typed-data digest == delegatorUserOpDigest(frozen op); each Solana message == frozen message, same order and count) and an unexpired review, then claims ONE signature claim for the whole group (claimAttempt purpose 'signature', attempt = group id). Expose it as a server action beside floFiSigningGate (flofi-wallet-action.ts:73). 4) Provider layer: flofi-evm-provider.ts gets a case 'eth_signTypedData_v4' that accepts only the delegator PackedUserOperation shape (primaryType, domain name EIP7702StatelessDeleGator v1, verifyingContract == own address, chainId in FLOFI_EVM_CHAINS, message.sender == own address, entryPoint == ENTRY_POINT_V0_7, initCode/paymasterAndData == '0x') AND a takeFloFiSigning binding, else 4200/4100. flofi-solana-wallet.ts:89 accepts 1..8 inputs only when the binding names a group flow (each input passes the same per-transaction checks), and returns N results each validated with signedSameTransaction. 5) Signer: requestThroughPrivy gets new cases. EVM: gate, then a new FloFiPrivy.signEvmTypedData (privy-context.tsx:19-46) implemented with useSignTypedData in privy-client.tsx, uiOptions {showWalletUIs:true, description from privyReview, buttonText 'Sign'}; then verify recoverUserOpSigner(chainId, op, sig) == address locally before returning. Solana: gate once, then N calls to privy.signSolanaTransaction, each labelled 'i of N', each checked. EmulatedPrivy/PrivyDriver (privy-client.tsx:167-223) and e2e/privy-emulator-client.js (signEvmTransaction 87, signSolanaTransaction 95) need the same methods. Arbitrary-payload safety comes from four layers: the provider-level shape filter, the mandatory binding, the server byte-equality against a FROZEN group artifact with a single claim, and local post-sign verification. Without a matching frozen group nothing reaches Privy.

answers.question: (3) How do injected EVM wallets get selected and chain-switched, and which EIP-1193 methods are already called (wallet_getCapabilities? wallet_sendCalls?)?
answers.answer: Selection: evm-discovery keeps EIP-6963 announcements for the page lifetime, one entry per provider object, and dispatches eip6963:requestProvider. An announcement claiming rdns xyz.flofi.wallet is ignored. Brave Wallet is excluded. A legacy window.ethereum (or ethereum.providers) is offered only when nothing announces, labelled 'Browser wallet' and never assumed to be MetaMask. FloFi Wallet providers are registered directly (registerManagedEvmProvider) and are never passive. The owner's explicit choice (chooseEvmWallet) is the only path that may prompt: build009 connectWith sends eth_requestAccounts to exactly that provider, then eth_chainId. A passive provider (remembered rdns, else a single MetaMask, else a single announced wallet; ambiguous means null) is used only for silent eth_accounts/eth_chainId. Chain switch: switchWalletNetwork sends wallet_switchEthereumChain. On 4902 it sends wallet_addEthereumChain from official parameters, for networks whose 'add' is non-null (Arbitrum's is null), switches again and requires eth_chainId to equal the target. signWorkflowGrant does its own switch (no add) before typed-data signing. Methods called today in app source (non-test): eth_chainId, eth_requestAccounts, eth_accounts, eth_sendTransaction (flow stores, sendRevocation), personal_sign (wallet proof, admin/dashboard sign-in, router stores), eth_signTypedData_v4 (delegation-browser signDelegation and signWorkflowGrant; cow-eip712 for a local test wallet only), wallet_switchEthereumChain, wallet_addEthereumChain, plus eth_getTransactionCount/eth_sendRawTransaction on FloFi's own/server paths. NOT called anywhere in apps/reference-dapp/src: wallet_getCapabilities, wallet_sendCalls, wallet_getCallsStatus, wallet_showCallsStatus, eth_signTransaction, wallet_grantPermissions. EIP-5792 exists only as the WIP parser packages/reference-compiler/src/eip5792.ts.

answers.question: (4) Wallet Standard Solana: which features does FloFi require; does signWithSolanaWallet accept several inputs; how are Phantom/Solflare detected?
answers.answer: Required: a wallet is listed for a cluster only if it advertises that chain plus 'standard:connect' and 'solana:signTransaction' (solanaWallets). The chosen account must list the chain and 'solana:signTransaction' (connectSolanaWallet, subscribeSolanaSession). 'solana:signMessage' is optional (Sign-In With Solana only). 'standard:events' and 'standard:disconnect' are used when present. 'solana:signAndSendTransaction' is deliberately never used (the module header says FloFi verifies the bytes before any broadcast). The legacy adapter method signAllTransactions is not used anywhere. signWithSolanaWallet(session, unsignedTransaction: string, prefix, assertCurrent?) takes ONE base64 transaction and calls feature.signTransaction with a single input, destructuring the first result. FloFi's local SignFeature type is already variadic, so a multi-input call needs no new type, only a new function. FloFi Wallet's own Wallet Standard wallet rejects inputs.length != 1. Detection: purely Wallet Standard registration (window 'wallet-standard:app-ready' / 'wallet-standard:register-wallet' handshake without an extra dependency). Wallets are identified by their registered name; the name 'FloFi Wallet' is reserved, and a third party announcing it is ignored. Phantom/Solflare/Backpack appear in KNOWN_WALLETS only to list them as 'Not detected' when absent. There is no window.phantom / window.solana / isPhantom probing. Privy's login modal separately lists phantom/solflare for sign-in (walletList) through toSolanaWalletConnectors, and that path is not used for signing. Whether Phantom/Solflare show ONE prompt for a multi-input solana:signTransaction is wallet behaviour that cannot be verified from repository or installed code. The @solana/wallet-standard-features package is not installed as a standalone package. Privy's own implementation shows it is legal for a wallet to prompt once per input.

answers.question: (5) Concrete plan: typed-data signing of a MetaMask 7702 delegator PackedUserOperation (MetaMask and, if possible, Privy); wallet_getCapabilities + wallet_sendCalls + wallet_getCallsStatus for MetaMask; multi-transaction Solana signing for Phantom/Solflare and FloFi Wallet; what Privy genuinely cannot do.
answers.answer: A) User operation, MetaMask/injected. Server precondition: eth_getCode(owner) == 0xef0100||DELEGATOR_IMPLEMENTATION on that chain (reuse account-code.ts classification or the drivers.ts:191 pattern); otherwise the group strategy falls back to EVM_WALLET_BATCH or EVM_OWNER_STEP. The server freezes the PackedUserOperation (nonceKeyOf(group), gas words = maximum charge, initCode '0x', paymasterAndData '0x', assertUserFundedOperation) and returns delegatorUserOpTypedData plus the decoded calls. Browser: add signUserOperation(address, chainId, typedData, expected) next to signWorkflowGrant in components/delegation-browser.ts, reusing its eth_chainId / wallet_switchEthereumChain / 4001 handling (67-78). Before asking the wallet it re-checks primaryType 'PackedUserOperation', domain {EIP7702StatelessDeleGator, '1', chainId, verifyingContract == address}, message.sender == address, entryPoint == ENTRY_POINT_V0_7, initCode/paymasterAndData == '0x', and decodeBatchCallData(message.callData) == the reviewed calls. It then sends eth_signTypedData_v4 [address, JSON] and posts {groupId, signature} to a server operation. That operation verifies verifyOwnerUserOpSignature against the FROZEN op (never a browser-supplied op) and only then queues bundler submission (user-funded/bundler.ts). B) User operation, FloFi Wallet (Privy). Signing the typed data is POSSIBLE with a Privy confirmation screen (useSignTypedData), wired as in answer (2). But a Privy EOA is a plain EOA (account-code.ts:5), and upgrading it to the delegator needs a 7702 authorization in a type-4 transaction. Privy offers that only through useSign7702Authorization, which uses headless raw-hash secp256k1_sign (no Privy screen, no uiOptions); its typed transaction request has no authorizationList, so the owner cannot sign and pay the type-4 transaction through Privy's confirmed path. Recommendation: do not call useSign7702Authorization or secp256k1_sign. Offer EVM_USER_OPERATION to a Privy wallet only if the server sees the delegator code already present; otherwise FloFi Wallet uses EVM_OWNER_STEP (one Privy confirmation per step), counted honestly. C) EIP-5792 for MetaMask: new browser module (e.g. wallet/wallet-calls.ts). (1) probe wallet_getCapabilities [address, [chainHex...]] -> eip5792.atomicCapability; treat errors 4100/4200/-32601 as unsupported; FloFi's provider already answers 4200 (flofi-evm-provider.ts:156); never request paymasterService or other capabilities. (2) Switch chain (switchWalletNetwork or the signWorkflowGrant pattern). (3) Compare the server's frozen calls with the reviewed calls in the browser (as verifyReviewedPayload does), then send wallet_sendCalls [eip5792.sendCallsRequest(chainId, from, calls)] (version 2.0.0, atomicRequired true). (4) Persist the returned id to the server immediately with sendCallsId; after this point any failure is UNKNOWN and is reconciled, never retried. (5) Poll wallet_getCallsStatus [id] -> callsStatus; report only tx hashes. The server re-reads each receipt and requires from == owner (gas payer S1), to == owner (self-call to execute) and that the decoded execute calldata equals the frozen calls; otherwise it fails closed. Map 4001 to rejected, and EIP-5792 errors 5700/5710/5740/5750 to fall back before signing. 'ready' = MetaMask performs the one-time upgrade inside the same confirmation, counted as one interaction plus an upgrade note. D) Solana multi-transaction, Phantom/Solflare: add signAllWithSolanaWallet(session, unsigned: string[], prefix, assertCurrent?) next to signWithSolanaWallet. It runs the same session/provider assertions, then makes ONE feature.signTransaction(...inputs) call with each input {account, transaction, chain} (1..8 inputs), requires result.length == N, copies each typed array (<=1232 bytes), and checks each is the same message with a non-zero slot-0 signature (move signedSameTransaction from flofi-solana-wallet.ts:51-57 into a shared helper). The server verifies each Ed25519 signature and message against the frozen group before the first submission. Count prompts as '1 (wallet-dependent)' only after confirming with the real wallets; otherwise state 1 call, up to N prompts. E) Solana multi-transaction, FloFi Wallet: the protocol/provider/gate changes in answer (2). Privy will show N confirmation screens (solana.mjs Ge loop), so the honest count is N Privy confirmations after one FloFi click. A cancel at transaction k leaves k-1 signed-but-unsubmitted transactions in the browser: drop them, and with durable nonces require a nonce advance before re-asking (see risks). WHAT PRIVY GENUINELY CANNOT DO (installed 3.51.0, embedded wallet): EIP-5792 wallet_sendCalls/getCapabilities/getCallsStatus (falls through to the public RPC); one-prompt multi-transaction Solana signing (N screens); a UI-confirmed EIP-7702 authorization (headless secp256k1_sign only) or a self-paid type-4 transaction through useSignTransaction (no authorizationList); smart wallets without a dashboard change and a new dependency (permissionless, not installed), and those are a different address and account type (not the MetaMask delegator).

risks: useSign7702Authorization and the embedded provider's secp256k1_sign sign arbitrary 32-byte hashes with no Privy confirmation. Exposing either (even indirectly through a generic EIP-1193 passthrough) would let page code sign anything with the user's key. FloFi must never route these methods.

Privy Solana multi-sign shows N screens. A cancel at screen k leaves k-1 valid signed transactions in browser memory. With recent blockhashes they expire in about 1-2 minutes; with DURABLE NONCES they stay valid until the nonce advances. Dropped bytes are only safe if they never left the page; a group cancel after partial signing must be recorded as UNKNOWN, and re-asking must first advance or verify the nonce.

MetaMask may relay wallet_sendCalls batches with 'gas fee tokens' or its own relayer (tx.from != owner). The server's S1 receipt check must refuse or flag such receipts, and the review must not claim 'you pay gas in ETH' if the wallet changed the payment method. Not verified.

eth_signTypedData_v4 of a PackedUserOperation is an authorization for a specific nonce and calls: if the server ever accepted a browser-supplied op instead of the frozen one, a malicious page could get the user to sign different calls under the same review. Always verify against the frozen op.

Privy useSignTypedData falls back to an EXTERNAL connected wallet when the address is not an embedded wallet (index-CaWn8tEz.mjs:33 signTypedData path calls a connected wallet's eth_signTypedData_v4). FloFi must keep the own(...) embedded-wallet check (privy-client.tsx:117) before calling it.
Wallet Standard multi-input prompt behaviour varies per wallet; claiming '1 signature' for Phantom/Solflare without manual verification would violate the honest-count requirement (S10).
